subtype: Waiting until it is too late [Actor]
passage: Thursday night. The statistics exam is on Monday and I have known since September that I don't understand regression. I hid it. When Maria asked in class how prep was going, I said “fine,” because saying the truth felt like showing everyone a stain. Now there are four days left and eleven topics that all rely on the one I never learned. Tonight I finally messaged Maria: “Can you help? I'm really behind.” The reply came in a minute: “Of course, but I wish you'd said so earlier. We can cover the main part this weekend, not everything.” My face burned reading it. Help is coming, but it is smaller than it would have been in October. — Asif

qa.q: On which day is the statistics exam?
qa.a: The statistics exam is on Monday.

qa.q: Why did Asif say “fine” when Maria asked how prep was going?
qa.a: Asif felt ashamed, and saying the truth felt like showing everyone a stain, so hiding it seemed safer.

qa.q: What could Asif do now with the four days left?
qa.a: Take the weekend session with Maria, focus on the main part of regression and ask about anything that stays unclear, accepting that not everything will be covered.

qa.q: How might Maria feel about the late request?
qa.a: Maria is probably kind but a little concerned, since “I wish you'd said so earlier” shows that Maria would have liked to help sooner.

grounding: A student hides falling behind until an exam is near and only then asks for help, and the delay makes help harder.

Rashmi: thank you. I should have asked in october
Karthik: yes. but tonight is tonight. come at 8, bring your notes
